newsitem.title: UK: Yugoslavia to resume debt talks with banks in July.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to resume debt talks with banks in July.

text.p: Yugoslavia's deputy prime minister Danko Djunic told Reuters after the second day of talks with creditor banks that the response to the country's debt restructuring proposal had been seen as "aggressive".
He said no settlement had yet been reached and that talks would resume in July with an invitation to host the talks in Belgrade.
According to official documents obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, Yugoslavia aims to restructure its $2.4 billion in debt with a syndicated loan.
Yugoslavia proposed to reduce the amount of principal and interest by 80 percent and issue $481 million via a syndicated loan with a 25-year maturity.
It is also proposing a grace period of nine years before repayment of principal begins.

When asked whether Yugoslavia would redraft the proposal in order to "please" the banks, Djunic replied: "We did not come here to please banks, we want to present a proposal which we can live with and not default on."
"We like to play by the rules of the market economy and we are not insisting on anything, but just on a deal that can survive the tests of time," he added.
He said he had offered to host the talks in Belgrade so that the banks' representatives could see "with their own eyes what is going on there".
"Nothing is yet settled, everything is still open (to discussion)," Djunic said.
"The grounds for the proposal is Yugoslavia's ability to pay in realistic terms based on realistic assumptions.
"We don't think we can possibly repay more than what we have offered, we wanted a syndicated loan but we can live with a bond as well."
